source.title: The Marginal Value of Momentum for Small Learning Rate SGD
source.authors: Run-Zhe Wang; Sadhika Malladi; Tianhao Wang; Kaifeng Lyu; Zhiyuan Li

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Some plotted values are not stated numerically in the text.
record.tranche_reason: Compares SGD and momentum SGD on validation or test performance under different training regimes; this is a conceptual test of optimizer-related generalization effects, not a direct test of the listed claim versions about adaptive optimizers.
record.gate_note: The study reports validation accuracy for ResNet-50 across batch sizes and test accuracy for ResNet-32 under standard training and SVAG noise scaling. The RoBERTa tables report downstream test performance for SGD and SGDM; those results compare momentum methods but do not test one of the mapped claim versions.
record.test_reason: Figure 1(b) compares ResNet-50 ImageNet validation accuracy across batch sizes under a common epoch-based schedule, bearing on V5. The stated result compares SGD with SGDM within batch sizes; it does not establish whether increasing batch size lowers accuracy within either optimizer.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors establish asymptotic equivalence under their small-learning-rate assumptions and find limited practical optimization and generalization benefits from momentum in noise-dominated settings. Momentum can help in large-batch settings permitting larger learning rates; SVAG shrinks or eliminates that advantage.
record.recipe_differences: Compares SGD with SGDM, including SVAG noise-scale changes; it does not reproduce the original studies or interventions in the mapped versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported optimizer comparison changes with batch size and with SVAG noise scaling ℓ; the paper also reports prompt-based and non-prompt fine-tuning settings for RoBERTa.

fits_no_version.finding: On ImageNet, SGD and SGDM perform comparably at smaller batch sizes; SGDM outperforms SGD at larger batches when using the learning rate selected for SGDM and its prescribed SGD conversion.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Momentum's performance advantage depends on batch size and effective learning rate.

fits_no_version.finding: For ResNet-32 on CIFAR-10 at batch size 512, standard SGD and SGDM achieve 89.35% and 92.68% test accuracy. With SVAG at ℓ = 4, they achieve 91.96% and 91.94%. Batch size remains fixed and the modified runs use more steps.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The SGD–SGDM performance difference can disappear when learning rates are reduced and gradient noise is increased through SVAG.

fits_no_version.finding: RoBERTa-large fine-tuning produces similar downstream test performance with SGD and SGDM across five tasks, with and without prompts.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Momentum offers limited downstream performance benefits in the tested language-model fine-tuning regimes.

record.problems: The batch-size accuracy results are shown in figures without numeric values stated in the text. The reported RoBERTa results average over five random subsets, but the paper's main comparison does not report training error alongside test performance.
record.rows_left_out: No rows extracted: the V5 batch-size result lacks batch-specific numerical values in the text, while the other results do not measure a mapped version. ResNet-50 batch-size results are in Figure 1; RoBERTa results are in Tables 1 and 2; ResNet-32 SVAG results are in Figure 2 and Appendix E.2.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting compared with natural-label held-out performance.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD; momentum SGD is not an adaptive optimizer.
Longer-training recovery, normalization or regularization changes, and large-batch language-model training. Learning-rate warmup is used, but its contribution is not isolated.
Dropout interventions and their dependence on training-set size or augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness ranking generalization gaps against other measures.
Removing memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: No rows were supplied. Figure 1(b)'s cross-batch accuracy values and trends cannot be recovered reliably from the supplied text, so no V5 verdict is justified. Comparable SGD and SGDM accuracy at a given batch size does not demonstrate comparable small- and large-batch accuracy. The omitted batch-size results are explicitly declared in rows_left_out, so they are not duplicated in missing.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Convolutional versus fully connected image models.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD or momentum SGD.

The paper varies batch size and reports validation accuracy, but its text does not provide batch-specific numerical outcomes that can be extracted as rows establishing the claimed large-batch penalty against smaller batches under a fixed epoch budget.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
